MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles.summary: Neither library has algebraic cycles modulo an adequate equivalence, correspondences, or any category of motives: 'Chow', 'motive', 'Tannakian category', 'numerical equivalence' and 'Weil cohomology' return no mathematical declaration in either tree. What is genuinely present and reusable is categorical rather than motivic: Mathlib's Karoubi envelope with its universal property (`CategoryTheory.Idempotents.karoubiUniversal`, `functorExtension`), rigid monoidal categories with duals, pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes, and an unquotiented cycle group with proper pushforward (`AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle.map`, functoriality unproved); Tau Ceti supplies pure and mixed Hodge structures with Tate twists, polarizations and semisimplicity, and a sorry-free Tannakian reconstruction of an affine group scheme from its category of finite-dimensional comodules (`TauCeti.Tannaka.tensorAutFunctor`). Everything specific to this roadmap — Chow groups, correspondence composition, pure and mixed motive categories, realizations and cycle classes, Jannsen semisimplicity, Nori's diagram category, motivic Galois groups and the cycle conjectures — is missing. The roadmap should also be reconciled with SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 and MotivicEtaleKTheory M.4/M.5a, which promise the same cycle and correspondence groups.

targets.target: Chow groups of smooth projective varieties (cycles modulo rational equivalence), graded
targets.note: Neither library defines a Chow group or rational equivalence of cycles. Mathlib's `AlgebraicCycle X R` is only the group of locally-finitely-supported functions on the points of a scheme (an unquotiented cycle group); grep for 'Chow' and 'rational equivalence' over both trees returns nothing mathematical. Tau Ceti's `WeilDivisor` tree has divisor classes and linear equivalence in codimension one only, and its `Dedekind/ClassGroup` file specialises further.

targets.target: Proper pushforward of cycles, with functoriality
targets.note: Mathlib defines pushforward `AlgebraicCycle.map` for a quasi-compact morphism, weighted by user-supplied dimension functions and the residue degree, and proves only `map_id`. Composition/functoriality `map_comp`, the projection formula and compatibility with any equivalence relation are absent; the file has four declarations in total and no `sorry`.

targets.target: Flat and refined (lci/Gysin) pullback of cycles
targets.note: No flat pullback, refined intersection or Gysin map for cycles in either library; `grep -rn -i 'flat pullback\|refined intersection\|Gysin'` over both Lean trees returns no declaration.

targets.target: External product of cycles and composition of correspondences via the triple product
targets.note: Correspondences of varieties do not exist in either library; the only `Correspondence` names in Mathlib are unrelated (order/graph theory).

targets.target: Associativity, diagonal identity, transpose and projection-formula compatibility for correspondences
targets.note: Depends on the previous target; nothing of the kind is present.

targets.target: Rational, algebraic, homological and numerical equivalence with the implication maps
targets.note: No adequate equivalence relation on cycles is defined. `numerical equivalence`, `homological equivalence` and `Weil cohomology` produce no hits in either tree.

duplicates.note: SF.5 'Intersection theory and Riemann-Roch' itself promises Chow groups, rational equivalence, proper pushforward, flat/lci pullback, refined Gysin maps and intersection products — the whole constructive core of MC.0. MC.0 lists SF.5 as its input, so the two layers must not both build the cycle groups.

M.4 constructs Bloch cycle complexes with the moving lemma, localisation, products, flat pullback and proper pushforward; the codimension-j cycle groups and their pullback/pushforward calculus are the same objects MC.0 states.
M.5a constructs finite correspondences and sheaves with transfers, overlapping MC.0's correspondence composition (and MC.4 declares M.5a as its input for exactly this reason).
S.7 builds Chern classes, the γ-filtration and 'the comparison with Chow groups in the regular setting', so it presupposes the same Chow-group construction.

targets.target: Additive category of correspondences of smooth projective varieties
targets.note: Requires MC.0's correspondence groups, which do not exist; no category of motives of any flavour is defined in either library.

targets.target: Idempotent completion (Karoubi envelope) of an additive/preadditive category
targets.note: `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi C` is the pseudo-abelian completion of an arbitrary category, with `toKaroubi` the canonical embedding, preadditive and finite-biproduct structure (`Biproducts.lean`), and idempotent-completeness of the result. This is strictly more general than the pseudo-abelian envelope of a correspondence category. No `sorry` in the `Idempotents` directory.

targets.target: Universal extension of additive functors through idempotent completion
targets.note: `karoubiUniversal : (Karoubi C ⥤ Karoubi D) ≅ (C ⥤ Karoubi D)` together with `functorExtension`, `functorExtension₁`, `karoubiUniversal₁` and `karoubiUniversal₂` are exactly the stated universal property, proved for arbitrary categories, so a fortiori for preadditive correspondence categories.

targets.target: Tensor product, dual, unit object on the motive category; Tate localization inverting the Lefschetz object
targets.note: Mathlib has the general theory of rigid (left/right dualizable) monoidal categories, and Tau Ceti has the Tate Hodge structure `ℤ(m)` and Tate twists of Hodge structures, but neither library has the Lefschetz motive, its inversion, or a monoidal structure on a category of motives.

targets.target: Explicit Chow–Künneth projectors for projective spaces and a pointed smooth projective curve, and projective-bundle decomposition
targets.note: No projective-bundle formula in any cohomology theory is present in either library (`grep -rn -i 'projective bundle'` returns nothing), and without Chow groups there are no projectors to exhibit.

duplicates.note: K.3's idempotent-completion of exact categories restates the same Karoubi-envelope construction that MC.1 asks for; both are already covered by Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Idempotents`.
M.5a constructs finite correspondences and effective motivic complexes, i.e. the correspondence category MC.1 idempotent-completes.

targets.target: Realization functors on a category of motives (Betti, de Rham, étale) for the admitted base fields
targets.note: There is no category of motives, hence no realization functor. The nearest carriers are Tau Ceti's category of mixed Hodge structures (a possible target of a Betti realization, built with no source functor) and Mathlib's pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of a scheme; neither is connected to cycles.

targets.target: Cycle class maps into a Weil cohomology
targets.note: No cycle class map exists; `grep -rn -i 'cycle class'` finds only Tau Ceti's Kummer-theory `cycleClass` names in `FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean`, which are unrelated Galois-cohomology classes of units.

targets.target: Compatibility of cycle classes with composition, cup products, pushforward, trace and Tate twists
targets.note: Depends on the previous target. Mathlib has no cup product or trace map on étale/ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes either — `EllAdicCohomology` is defined as a sheaf-cohomology group with no ring structure developed.

targets.target: Betti/de Rham comparison for an embedding into ℂ, and étale realization compared with its comparison suppliers
targets.note: Neither algebraic de Rham cohomology of a variety nor singular cohomology of the analytification is constructed in either library, so there is no comparison to prove. Tau Ceti's Hodge package supplies the linear-algebra target only.

duplicates.note: PS.0 builds Betti/de Rham realization comparison matrices, Hodge filtration and Tate twists for motives and names MC.2 as its input; the realization interface is stated in both.
M.4's motivic cohomology and its comparisons cover the cycle-class-to-cohomology maps in the higher-Chow formulation.
GH.1 constructs the étale cycle class and Abel–Jacobi map plus the de Rham/syntomic realization for its own cycles, duplicating MC.2's cycle-class compatibility statements in a special case.

targets.target: The rational category of numerical motives as a quotient of Chow motives
targets.note: Numerical equivalence is not defined in either library, so the quotient category does not exist.

targets.target: Finite-dimensionality of numerical correspondence spaces via a Weil cohomology
targets.note: No Weil cohomology is available in either library to bound the correspondence spaces.

targets.target: Decomposition of endomorphism algebras/idempotents and Jannsen's semisimple abelian theorem
targets.note: Mathlib has semisimplicity for modules and rings (`RingTheory/Semisimple`) but no notion of semisimple abelian category (`CategoryTheory/Preadditive/HomOrthogonal.lean` says such a definition is still 'preliminary'). Tau Ceti proves the analogous semisimplicity for polarizable pure Hodge structures, which is a different theorem about a different category.

duplicates.note: MC.7's 'standard conjectures' register restates the homological-versus-numerical equivalence question that MC.3 must keep separate; the two layers must share one definition of numerical equivalence.

targets.target: Finite correspondences and Nisnevich sheaves with transfers
targets.note: Neither library has finite correspondences or presheaves with transfers; the Nisnevich topology itself is only mentioned in a comment in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/MayerVietorisSquare.lean` and is not defined.

targets.target: The derived/localized category DM, A¹-invariance and Tate stabilization, geometric subcategory
targets.note: Mathlib has general derived categories and Bousfield-style localization of categories, but no motivic homotopy category, no A¹-localization and no Tate spectrum.

targets.target: Localization, homotopy invariance and projective-bundle comparison in DM
targets.note: Nothing of the kind exists.

targets.target: Identification of higher Chow/motivic cohomology with the DM mapping groups
targets.note: Higher Chow groups are not defined in either library.

targets.target: Motives of A¹, G_m and projective space; the boundary map for a closed point of a smooth curve
targets.note: Depends on the whole construction; absent.

duplicates.note: M.5a is declared an input and states the same targets verbatim — finite correspondences, Nisnevich sheaves with transfers, A¹-localization, effective motivic complexes and cancellation.
M.4 owns Bloch's higher Chow groups and motivic cohomology, which MC.4 asks to identify with DM mapping groups; the motivic-cohomology definition must not be duplicated.
LD.3 ('Motivic integration and transfer') consumes MC.4 and restates a Grothendieck-ring-of-varieties/motivic-measure layer over the same geometric input.

targets.target: Endomorphism coalgebra of a finite diagram representation and its filtered colimit
targets.note: Mathlib has coalgebras, comodules and Hopf algebras, and Tau Ceti has finite comodule categories, but the diagram/quiver-representation endomorphism coalgebra of Nori's construction is not built in either.

targets.target: The Nori diagram category and its universal factorization property
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'nori'` over both Lean trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Homology of algebraic pairs, boundary morphisms and the long exact sequence of a triple
targets.note: Tau Ceti has singular homology of topological pairs in `AlgebraicTopology/Singular`, but relative singular cohomology of an algebraic pair (X,Y) as a functor on Nori's diagram is not constructed.

targets.target: Tensor and duality structure on the Nori category; Betti and de Rham fibre functors
targets.note: Absent; algebraic de Rham cohomology of a variety does not exist in either library.

targets.target: The comparison functor from geometric motives to Nori motives
targets.note: Neither category exists.

duplicates.note: PS.2 compares the algebra of formal periods with 'the coordinate ring of the Nori period torsor', so it consumes the same Nori construction; MC.5/MC.6 must own it once.

targets.target: The group functor of tensor automorphisms of a fibre functor on a neutral Tannakian category
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds `Tannaka.tensorAutFunctor`, the functor sending a commutative algebra A to the tensor automorphisms of the scalar-extended forgetful functor on finite-dimensional comodules over a Hopf algebra H, and proves it is represented by H (`fgPointTensorIsoEquiv`, `reconstructedPoint`), sorry-free. What is missing is the abstract input: there is no definition of a (neutral) Tannakian category, so the construction is only available when the category is already presented as comodules over a given Hopf algebra.

targets.target: Torsor of tensor isomorphisms between two fibre functors
targets.note: Only automorphisms of a single fibre functor are constructed in Tau Ceti; no Isom-torsor between two distinct fibre functors, and no proof that it is a torsor, exists in either library.

targets.target: Finite-diagram approximation and pro-algebraic reconstruction of the Tannakian group
targets.note: Tau Ceti's reconstruction is for a single Hopf algebra, not a filtered colimit over finite subdiagrams; Mathlib's `autMulEquivAutGalois` does the analogous pro-representability for Galois categories — `Aut F` is the inverse limit of the automorphism groups of pointed Galois objects, which is the profinite, not the pro-algebraic, statement.

targets.target: Artin and Tate subcategories and their tensor automorphism groups; export of period torsors
targets.note: No category of motives, hence no Artin or Tate subcategory; period torsors are absent.

duplicates.note: GS4:integral-dual-group constructs a total-cohomology fibre functor, proves exactness/faithfulness/tensor compatibility and reconstructs its affine group scheme — the same Tannakian reconstruction machinery MC.6 states, in the Satake category.
RF4:G-torsors ('Tannakian transfer') transports structures along a tensor functor using the same torsor-of-fibre-functors formalism.
PS.2 consumes MC.6 and restates the Nori period torsor and its coordinate ring.
IG.0 owns Galois categories and fibre functors; the pro-representability half of MC.6's reconstruction is the same argument in the profinite setting (and is already in Mathlib for Galois categories).

targets.target: Typed statements of the Hodge, Tate and standard conjectures
targets.note: Neither library states any of these conjectures; `grep -rn -i 'hodge conjecture\|tate conjecture\|standard conjecture'` over both Lean trees returns nothing. Tau Ceti's Hodge package supplies Hodge structures and Tate twists but no notion of Hodge class of a cycle.

targets.target: Bloch–Beilinson filtrations and motivic t-structures as typed statements
targets.note: Absent; there is no t-structure API on any triangulated category in either library (`TStructure` hits are Tau Ceti's exact structures on module categories, an unrelated notion).

targets.target: A theorem register separating known classes of varieties and coefficients from the general conjecture
targets.note: Bookkeeping over statements that do not exist.

targets.target: Proved special cases: divisor/Lefschetz (1,1), curve and abelian-variety cases
targets.note: No special case is proved. Tau Ceti's divisor theory (`WeilDivisor`, `CartierDivisor`, Abel–Jacobi for curves) and its polarizable-Hodge-structure semisimplicity are the closest carriers, but none states a cycle-class surjectivity theorem.

duplicates.note: MC.3's Jannsen theorem is the one unconditional result in this circle of ideas; MC.7 must state the conjectural homological-equals-numerical half separately.

T1 explicitly warns that its absolute-Hodge/tensor input 'is a proved dependency, not an assumption that the Hodge conjecture holds', so the typed Hodge-conjecture statement MC.7 owns is consumed there.
DM.5 proves the Tate theorem for Drinfeld modules — a function-field analogue of the Tate conjecture case MC.7 registers.
